findings.title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy values
findings.body: The same $alignment value is written to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align. Those legacy properties use different keywords (start/end/center/baseline) than modern flexbox, so values such as flex-start or flex-end are invalid there. The mixin is called with center and baseline, which happen to work. Also, -ms-align-items is not a real property, and the line at 120 has trailing whitespace.

findings.title: order mixin maps value to ordinal-group without offset
findings.body: The legacy box-ordinal-group property starts at 1, while the modern `order` property defaults to 0. Passing the same value to both gives different relative ordering in old engines. The mixin does not translate between them.

findings.title: Header flex layout removes .title float and relies on order and auto margin
findings.body: .contents becomes a flex container, but children such as .title lose their float rules. Float is ignored on flex items anyway. The panel now uses margin-left:auto plus order(3), while the extra-info wrapper uses order(2). Other siblings that have no explicit order, such as the logo and the mobile header, default to 0 and are unaffected. Any child that still depends on float or inline layout, for example the .valign-helper with height:100%, will now behave differently as a flex item. This is a risky layout change with no test or visual verification.

findings.title: clear:both on a flex container and floats inside flex items
findings.body: .small-action is now display:flex, but its children (.topic-avatar, button, .avatar) still use float. Floats have no effect on flex items. The `clear: both` on the container is also redundant. The padding and margin changes (padding: 0 1.5% replacing the 4em left indent) alter the visual layout of small actions, and the avatar spacing is now inconsistent.
